transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

It is very unlikely to be about to break. Induction hobs work by creating a magnetic field that makes the metal in your pan vibrate at high frequency; this often causes a humming or buzzing noise, especially with large, heavy stockpots on high power. This is normal behaviour for induction technology. However, if you hear loud cracking, smell burning plastic, see sparks, or if the hob switches off with an error code, then it would be a fault.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Thanks, that's reassuring. No error codes or burning smell, it still heats fine, just noisy. It started when I bought a new budget stockpot last month - is that likely to be the cause?

Yes, that is probably the cause. Induction hobs only work with ferromagnetic pans (those containing iron or steel). Cheaper stockpots often have thinner bases, different alloy mixes, or poor magnetic coupling compared to quality cookware. This mismatch causes the magnetic field to 'vibrate' more aggressively against the pan base, creating that loud buzzing sound you are hearing. Since it heats fine and there are no error codes, your hob is perfectly healthy; you just need a better-quality pot for high-power cooking.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Incompatible or thin-bottomed pan causing excessive vibration (medium)
